diagram.alt: Graph drawn on x and y axes; 2 plotted lines, curves or sets of points are drawn; some of the plotted lines are dashed. Labels shown: 3-(square root of 3), 3+(square root of 3). Marked on the horizontal axis: 3-(square root of 3), 3+(square root of 3); vertical axis: minus 1. Read the question for what it asks.

manual.title: Horizontal stretch of a parabola by three
manual.prompt: The graph of $y=x^{2}-2x$ is dilated horizontally by a factor of $3$. Find the new equation, its $x$-intercepts and vertex.

manual.title: Exponential from its asymptote and two points
manual.prompt: The graph of $y=a\cdot2^{x}+k$ has horizontal asymptote $y=3$ and passes through $(1,5)$. Find $a$ and $k$, and check that $(2,7)$ lies on it.

diagram.alt: Graph drawn on x and y axes; 2 plotted lines, curves or sets of points are drawn; some of the plotted lines are dashed. Marked on the horizontal axis: 1, 2; vertical axis: 3, 5, 7. Read the question for what it asks.

manual.title: Image of a point under two dilations
manual.prompt: The point $(3,-2)$ lies on $y=f(x)$. Find the corresponding point on $y=4f\left(\tfrac x2\right)$.

manual.title: First maximum of three sine two x
manual.prompt: The graph of $y=\sin x$ is dilated vertically by factor $3$ and horizontally by factor $\tfrac12$. Write the new equation and find the image of the maximum $\left(\tfrac\pi2,1\right)$.

manual.title: Root of four x as two different dilations
manual.prompt: Show that $y=\sqrt{4x}$ can be obtained from $y=\sqrt x$ by a horizontal dilation or by a vertical dilation, giving each factor.
